axes.model_access: In-house speech models: official docs list s2.1-pro (production), s2-pro, s2.1-pro-free (zero-cost testing tier) and drama-3 (plain-language direction with sounds, pauses and tags), with s1 marked for retirement on 2026-12-31; self-hosting runs on the fish_speech repo (2026-11-21).
axes.runtime: Cloud API at `https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts` (plus `/model` for voice creation) and the fish.audio web app; official self-hosting docs provide a local GPU inference server (`localhost:8080/v1/tts`), so one integration can target cloud or self-hosted (2026-11-21).
axes.local_files: Self-hosting keeps both weights and audio local: official docs walk through semantic tokens to DAC decoding on local hardware, writing output files; the cloud path returns bytes or stream chunks, with voice models stored account-side (2026-11-21).
axes.background: Synthesis is synchronous or streaming: `tts.convert()` returns complete audio, `tts.stream()` emits chunks and WebSocket accepts live text. Voice training is an async state machine, with a new model moving from created to trained (fast mode is usually immediate) and retries on failure (2026-11-21).
axes.tools: TTS (multilingual, mp3/wav/pcm/opus, speed 0.5–2.0), instant cloning with reference audio plus transcript, persistent voice models (`POST /model`, private/unlist/public), the Voice Library and Drama 3 direction tags. The Voice Cloning page also lists Professional Voice Clone (verified, web only) (2026-11-21).
axes.context: No conversational memory: each TTS request is independent, and voices are reused via `reference_id`; instant cloning passes the sample with the request, while persistent cloning trains a voice id, so the asset is a cross-request consistency mechanism rather than session context (2026-11-21).
axes.permissions: API key (`FISH_API_KEY`) plus account/subscription. Clone samples must be the user’s own voice or authorised; Professional Voice Clone is listed as a verified tier. Public voices enter the Voice Library only when the user chooses private, unlist or public (2026-11-21).
axes.fit: Fit: fast cloning of one’s own voice, consistent brand voice, real-time assistants (about 300 ms to first audio in balanced mode) and self-hosted offline synthesis. Not fit: cloning someone else’s voice (a consent red line), enterprise audit chains, or direct mainland access (measured 000) (2026-11-21).

related: The two cloning-oriented titans: ElevenLabs carries a heavier enterprise-compliance narrative, fish audio a heavier community voice ecosystem.
Also China-background cloning lines: MiniMax connects directly + is API-heavy, fish audio needs a network path + is community-heavy.
Downstream of cloned voices: voices replicated by fish audio often feed HeyGen-class avatar platforms for narration (cross-linked after filing).
Up/downstream of the audio pipeline: Whisper transcribes in, fish audio synthesizes out — often the two ends of the same voice pipeline.
